entries.message: <{tag}> has an async connectedCallback or an async setup, which cannot be awaited during a synchronous render — its markup would be empty.
entries.fix: Use renderToStringAsync, or load data first and pass it as attributes.

entries.message: `attributes` cannot serve {name} — an on… attribute runs its value as code in the browser, and a value bound into one in a template is dropped for that reason.
entries.fix: Write the handler in the component — a static attribute in its template, or an @event binding.

entries.message: `attributes` cannot use {name} as a name — a name written into the served tag may not be empty or hold whitespace, a quote, a backtick, "<", "/", "=", ">" or a control character: the rule a spread's keys follow, on the client and the server.
entries.fix: Give it a valid attribute name.

entries.message: a `<![CDATA[` inside an SVG or MathML element whose content is HTML (`title`, `desc`, `foreignObject`, `mtext`, …), or in a template serialized at a bare foreign depth, could end at its first `>` (as a bogus comment, once an HTML element is open) or at `]]>` (in SVG), and the two readings disagree here — so it is refused rather than guessed.
entries.fix: Keep `>` out of the section before its `]]>`, or write the text without a CDATA section.

entries.message: binds `{name}` on a <font> inside <svg> or <math>: the client builds that <font> as SVG or MathML, while the browser's parse of the served page leaves the <svg> or <math> at it (HTML's rule for a <font> with `color`, `face` or `size`), so the two pages' trees differ.
entries.fix: SVG's <font> is obsolete: style text with `fill` and `font-family`, or close the <svg> before an HTML <font>. Said once per template.

entries.message: a "{type}" listener threw — the dispatch went on, as in a browser; its error follows.
entries.fix: The error names what went wrong. This is said once per component and event type for the life of the process.

entries.message: some of this element's markup could not be parsed, so children/querySelector do not see it — they answer emptily, or with only the part that did parse.
entries.fix: This DOM parses markup it can reproduce exactly and declines the rest, rather than building a tree the browser would not — a mismatched or stray closing tag is the usual cause. Make the markup well-formed, or build the children with createElement/appendChild if a component needs to read them back.

entries.message: parsed {written}, a named character reference this server reads back as written (it decodes six names itself), while a browser decodes it: what a server component reads from that markup differs from what the browser shows. The served markup is unchanged.
entries.fix: Wire the HTML Standard's whole table before the first render: `wire([namedReferences])`, from @verajs/ssr/named-references. A template rendered before the wire keeps the name as written. Said once per name.

entries.message: component nesting exceeded {max} levels. A component that renders itself recurses without bound, and on a server that is a hung request — so this refuses rather than waiting for the stack to go.
entries.fix: If the tree is genuinely this deep it renders fine in a browser, which has no such limit; that difference is in the @verajs/ssr README.

entries.message: no custom element definition found for {url}.
entries.fix: Export the component's class from that module, or pass { tag }.

entries.message: `{name}` must be {expected}.
entries.fix: Check the options passed to renderToString.

entries.message: {name} is not an option of renderToString, so it would configure nothing.
entries.fix: The options are {options}.

entries.message: a `<plaintext>` never ends — no end tag closes it, so everything after it on the page would be its text.
entries.fix: Remove it; to show markup as text, render it as a string inside a `<pre>`.

entries.message: this process has working web storage — Node 26 gives every process a sessionStorage shared by every request, and --localstorage-file adds a localStorage — and components render against the process's own globals: a `typeof sessionStorage` or `typeof localStorage` guard passes here, and a component can render one visitor's stored state into markup served to everyone.
entries.fix: Guard per-user state with `isServer` from @verajs/core (`if (!isServer()) …`) rather than a `typeof` test of the storage. Said once per process, in every build.

entries.message: <{tag}> refused a value from `props` — setting it threw {thrown}.
entries.fix: A read-only property cannot be set; pass it as an attribute, or give the class a setter. The setter's own error is this one's cause.

entries.message: <{tag}> threw while rendering{others} — its markup would be empty: {thrown}.
entries.fix: The component's own error is this one's cause.

entries.message: the server renderer has been replaced — a renderer was wired that does not know @verajs/ssr is rendering, and every component would render empty.
entries.fix: Import @verajs/ssr BEFORE wiring the renderer: vera's renderer then declines on the server and keeps only its shadow default. A renderer that is not vera's: guard its wiring with `isServer` from @verajs/core (`if (!isServer())`).

entries.message: a value in a <script> is code — on a served page it runs — so a script hole is refused, except in a JSON data block (its type ends in `json`, with no character reference).
entries.fix: Give the script a JSON type (`type="application/json"` or `application/ld+json`) for state or JSON-LD, or pass the value another way.

entries.message: a bound <select> {binding} matched none of its {count} options: the client shows none selected, and the served page shows its first.
entries.fix: Markup cannot say "none selected". Give every value the select can be bound to an option (`<option value="">` for no choice yet), or mark one `selected` yourself. Said once per template.

entries.message: this DOM cannot answer the selector {selector} — {why}.
entries.fix: It matches on structure and attributes only; rather than return a wrong answer it says so.

entries.message: <{tag}> refused the bound property `.{name}` — its setter threw {thrown}.
entries.fix: The binding's value is the argument it was given; the setter's own error is this one's cause.

entries.message: CSSStyleSheet.deleteRule needs a parsed rule list; this sheet is text.
entries.fix: Remove the rule from the text instead, or replace the sheet.

entries.message: this render declared itself static, so its stores are not reactive and writing {prop} would change nothing.
entries.fix: Remove `static: true` from renderToString, or stop writing to the store during the render.

entries.message: hoisted different CSS than it did on an earlier render, and the new stylesheet was dropped.
entries.fix: A tag's styles are established once per class for the life of the process, so CSS that varies per request cannot be hoisted — put the varying part in an inline style or a custom property instead.

entries.message: a template cannot render inside a text-only element (`<style>`, a JSON `<script>`, `<title>`, `<textarea>`, or never-shown content: `<noscript>`, `<iframe>`) — its content is text.
entries.fix: Render a string there; a list of strings is joined.

entries.message: was served after its {timeout} ms `timeout` with a promise still pending in {pendingIn} (an async setup or connectedCallback, or a promise a frame callback returned), so the page is what had rendered by then. Still waiting on customElements.whenDefined for {waitingOn}, which the server never defined.
entries.fix: If only the browser defines it, return before that wait on the server — `if (isServer()) return;`, `isServer` from @verajs/core — so the server serves what the component shows before the wait, as the browser does first. Raise `timeout` if the wait is real, or find the promise that never settles. Said once per component for the life of the process.

entries.message: a template cannot end inside a tag — the client drops an unfinished tag.
entries.fix: Close the tag inside the template.

entries.message: refused {href} — it resolves outside {root}.
entries.fix: Nothing was imported. A module URL is bounded to `base`; point it at a module inside that directory.
